assays.assay_description: 60-min recording in a Plexiglas chamber (30.5 x 61 x 38 cm) with 8 wall holes and 3 floor holes, infrared beams tracking position, rearing, and holepokes. Measures: distance travelled, centre duration, rearings, holepokes, jumps, freezing duration, and defecations. Tested with DOM, mescaline, psilocin, 25CN-NBOH, lisuride, TBG, +/- M100907 pretreatment.

application_type.evidence: All drugs were administered intraperitoneally at a volume of 10 mL per 1 kg mouse bodyweight.

setup_habituation.evidence: The experimental animals were acclimated to the experimental environment for 3 days before behavioural testing (room acclimation, not apparatus habituation specified).

setup_restrain.evidence: The mice were allowed to explore the mouse BPM for 60 min.

food_restriction.evidence: free access to water and food provided at the top of the cage (in home cage); no food in BPM apparatus during 60-min test.

water_restriction.evidence: free access to water and food provided at the top of the cage (in home cage); no water in BPM apparatus during the test.

time_to_assay.evidence: Ten minutes after administration of DOM, mescaline, psilocin, 25CN-NBOH, lisuride, or TBG; or 30 min after administration of M100907, the animals were placed in the mouse BPM.

outcomes.summary: DOM, mescaline, and psilocin reduced locomotor activity at high doses and influenced rearings in a characteristic inverted U-shaped dose-response function. The hallucinogenic 5-HT2A agonist 25CN-NBOH produced similar effects, while the nonhallucinogenic agonists lisuride and TBG failed to increase rearing. M100907 (5-HT2A antagonist) pretreatment reversed DOM- and 25CN-NBOH-induced increases in rearings and jumps, but not holepokes. Discriminant analysis distinguished hallucinogens from non-hallucinogens, with rearing being the most discriminative variable.
outcomes.statistics: DOM distance: F(8,105)=30.42, p<0.0001; DOM rearing: F(8,104)=34.33, p<0.0001; DOM jumps: chi2=61.15, p<0.0001; mescaline rearing: F(7,93)=7.770, p<0.0001; psilocin distance: F(7,106)=27.22, p<0.0001; psilocin rearing: Treatment x Block F(7,95)=9.577, p<0.0001; 25CN-NBOH rearing: F(5,67)=5.758, p=0.0002; lisuride distance: F(3,36)=83.94, p<0.0001; TBG distance: F(4,55)=20.44, p<0.0001; M100907 x DOM rearing: F(1,11)=30.31, p=0.0002.
outcomes.evidence: DOM influenced rearing and jumps, with an increase in exploratory activity at low to moderate doses and a decrease at higher doses, following a bell-shaped dose-response function.

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed the study used a single behavioural paradigm (the mouse BPM); consolidated into one assay entry as per the rubric (different drugs and antagonist pretreatments = one assay).
